key_insight: Doubling urinary cadmium was associated with 1.71–1.92 years shorter survival at the 10th percentile, with smaller differences at later survival percentiles.
clinical_relevance: The findings support population-level efforts to reduce cadmium exposure but do not establish causality or guide individual prognosis.
method: Linked NHANES 1999–2014 data for US adults aged 40 or older to mortality records through 2019.
Used weighted censored quantile regression at the 10th, 25th, and 50th survival percentiles, adjusting for confounders across five imputations.
Measured blood lead and mercury and urinary cadmium and arsenic; urinary-metal analyses required preserved kidney function.
evidence_signal: Among 24,338 adults, 6,992 died; cadmium associations in 7,061 participants persisted after lead adjustment, whereas lead associations did not persist after cadmium adjustment.
watch_item: Observational associations may reflect residual confounding, particularly the apparent longer survival associated with mercury.
paper_title: Environmental toxic metal exposure and conditional mortality survival among US adults: a prospective cohort study
